text_post: Just wondering how much you let it impact your life? For me its a big contributor on the quality of my life. Right now, my life as a whole is going okay, nothing great. She said she isn't focused on a relationship right now for personal reasons(work, learning to be happy with herself, etc etc) and so far, she has been sticking to her word.  Be that as it may, it doesn't make my life better because no matter what I do, I can't get a woman to see me past a platonic friend, so I have to force myself to find ways to live with it, though that's easier said than done. I never let my dating troubles control me until my mid-twenties. Before than it was a minor nuisance, yet the longer this went on, the more "no's" I got, along with peers making fun of me for it, its made me borderline suicidal that I nearly committed myself for it. Its a good thing my couple friends let me stay at their place for a few days to look over me because its likely I would've been institutionalized, and that's still a possibility if this goes untreated by the time I reach 35. So does anybody here have this same trouble with their sexless/dateless life to where they can't focus on anything else? If so, how do you combat it(other than someone agreeing to fuck you)? Thanks.

author: alone99
text_post: It's controlled my life ever since I was in my 20's. The desire to make love to a woman and have a girlfriend has haunted me for as long as I can remember. Every time I thought I might have had a chance (only to find out they never saw me as anything more than the Nice Guy), I was shot down and forced back into reality. I wake up every day and immediately think, "I'm still a virgin at 57." It's inconceivable to me. I see beautiful women every day as I go about my low-status job and/or errands, and it's just a reminder of what I'll never have. As a matter of fact, because I'm a musician and songwriter, I actually have a whole litany of self-hate songs that run through my head all the time. Some I wrote on the spot, others were written before most of you were born. I've never recorded any of these "songs" because I would probably be committed to a mental hospital if anyone heard them.  When I was 31, I called a radio talk show (the Jim Bohannon Show) whose topic for the evening was dating and how to meet people. His guest was a woman who had written a book on the topic. I explained to her that, despite my best efforts, I was still a virgin and wanted to figure out what I was doing wrong. One of the things she told me was, "You're not defined by your virginity!" And then of course she told me to "keep getting out there." Well, if I were to speak to her now some 25 years later, I'm sure she would agree that my incel and virginity most definitely define me. I don't wear a sign around my neck that announces it to the world, but I think it's pretty obvious. I also see other losers like myself schlogging around stores and parking lots who look as if they've never been with a woman either.  At least I still attempt to meet up with people and get involved with those who have common interests. But most of the time no one is available because they have such "busy" schedules.  The hardest part for me is accepting the fact that no woman has ever seen me as attractive enough to want anything more than a casual friendship. It's emasculating and makes me the ultimate beta male. But even now, I don't even have that. There are no women in my life and haven't been for nearly ten years. I occasionally speak to women on jobs that I work, but that's a completely different environment. And even then, it never goes past a business relationship. author: silvereagle
text_post: Just yesterday, seemingly by chance,  I came across a mention of a famous 20th century Portuguese poet, writer, critic and translator Fernando Pessoa (1888 - 1935) who I had never heard of before. Died a virgin at 47, drank himself to death. How did he cope? He didn't of course. Had a strange life, living in relatives' homes or renting small rooms, barely making a living as a translator. He pined for women. A genius, he left many projects unfinished, and I think his incel played a part here. He became obsessed with the occult and would hold seances in which the spirits would berate him for his virginity, calling him a man without a prick! Like others, I take a skeptical view and think the 'spirits' who communicated to him were just the voices from his own subconscious mind. He was like almost all male middle-aged virgins, clearly filled with shame and self-loathing. I am 48, I have now outlived Pessoa in age. How have I coped? Especially when I had no outlet into writing and poetry, as Pessoa did. And he is recognized as a giant figure in Portuguese letters. And yet his inceldom broke him utterly. Well I haven't coped. I have at least one foot in the abyss of madness. As the famous French poet Charles Baudelaire put it - who himself may well have died a virgin at 46! Nobody can be sure - 'I can feel the wind of the wings of madness'.
